title: Rabies reports are rising in California. The reason why is a mystery

analysis.time: Rabies reports are up across the United States this year, including in one greater Bay Area county where human exposures to rabid animals have tripled, prompting a local advisory to stay away from sick or injured creatures.
analysis.location_and_population: California, United States; Santa Cruz County, California.
analysis.event: Rabies reports are rising, prompting local advisories to stay away from sick or injured creatures. The reason for the increase is unknown.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Nationally, rabies inquiries after potential exposure are up 17% this year. In Santa Cruz County, nine rabid bats have been identified so far this year, compared to three in the previous two years. Post-exposure prophylaxis use has increased.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Investigation into the cause of the increase is ongoing. Public health officials advise vaccination of pets and caution against approaching wild animals, especially if they appear sick or injured.

analysis.brief_en: Rabies reports are increasing in California, with nine rabid bats identified in Santa Cruz County this year, up from three in the previous two years. The rise is unexplained, but public health officials advise vaccination of pets and caution against approaching wild animals, especially if they appear sick or injured. Nationally, rabies inquiries after potential exposure are up 17% this year.
